conventions.convention: Entropy is finite and measured in J/K. Concavity and continuity apply on specified convex regions; C² regularity and finite positive S_U apply only on designated open single-phase charts. Physical-coordinate derivatives include the fixed SI conversion factors.
Tagged scaling changes c to c^(λ); tagged entropy scaling alone does not assert homogeneity of one fixed constitutive function.
The common-law branch additionally requires a nonempty open positive cone, all positive scalings, and coordinate-preserving entropy transport with common species, units, and reference conventions.
The feasible set records exactly the declared totals, retained barriers, and permitted exchanges; it need not be nonempty, compact, convex, or contain a maximizer.
Stable equilibrium implies an attained global entropy maximum on the exact feasible set. The postulate asserts neither the converse classification, uniqueness, nor relaxation dynamics.
Reversibility is relative to the declared boundary and protocol: an admitted reverse record restores auxiliary/device states and reverses every signed boundary transfer.
Thermal-contact equilibrium relates tagged states within the declared family and protocol convention. Equivalence is separately postulated and supplies no numerical thermometer scale.

The second law compares equilibrium endpoint constituent tuples in the same feasible set, includes all entropy-changing constituents, and assigns no entropy to intermediate nonequilibrium configurations. Irreversibility alone does not require strict entropy increase.

load_bearing.statement: For each admitted material constitution c, adopt a finite entropy S_c on D_c; it is continuous and concave on specified convex regions, additive under the admitted separated-system composition map, C² with finite positive S_U on designated open single-phase charts, and satisfies S_{c^(λ)}(δ_λ x)=λS_c(x) for admitted tagged scalings.

An equilibrium feasible set is the model-declared subset of the product of constituent equilibrium state domains satisfying the specified totals and exactly the declared exchange permissions and retained constraints. No existence, compactness, convexity, uniqueness, or attainment assumption is imposed.

Any endpoint tuple classified as stable equilibrium under the fixed totals, retained partitions, and permitted exchanges belongs to the exact feasible set and attains the global maximum of the summed constituent entropy there.

A thermal-contact family consists of tagged equilibrium states. Its declared diathermal contact permits thermal energy transfer while forbidding matter transfer and mechanical or composition work across that contact; thermal-contact equilibrium is defined relative to the declared contact preparation and protocol.

On the designated open positive-cone branch, adopt coordinate-preserving entropy transport from each scaled-system chart to the fixed material-law chart. Combined with tagged entropy scaling, this gives S_c(λx)=λS_c(x) for every x in that cone and λ>0.

concerns.concern: Verification 1.1 claims, “Thus the model satisfies [F1]–[F6],” but the adopted compound composition and entropy additivity are incompatible with the example. Every φ(x) has the same total U, total V, and aligned species amounts. By post-td-bulk-additivity, κ_AB(φ(x)) therefore has the same complete coordinate tuple in the fixed D_{c_{A⊔B}} for every x. The state-domain definition identifies states with the same tuple. Consequently S_{A⊔B}(κ_AB(φ(x))) must be constant, whereas the entropy postulate requires it to equal S_A+S_B=s_*(1+x). Taking x=1/4 and x=3/4 gives different required values at the same compound state. The scalar supremum calculation is correct, but the claimed thermodynamic model satisfying these prerequisites does not exist as written.

Verification 1.1 invokes [F4] and [F5] to identify the admitted compound entropy with s_*(1+x). However, all listed feasible partitions have identical total U, V, and aligned mole amounts, so post-td-bulk-additivity maps them to the same coordinate tuple in the fixed compound state domain. Entropy as a function on that domain must have one value there. Additivity instead requires values 13s_*/10 and 19s_*/10 at the feasible partitions x=3/10 and x=9/10. Thus the relative-local and global maximum calculation is valid for the displayed function on the product, but the example cannot simultaneously satisfy its declared aggregate-state composition and entropy-additivity prerequisites.

The Definition starts with any “admitted closed process record” and then evaluates Q[P], W_on[P], and their reverse-record values. Its supplier def-td-process-and-protocol defines these functionals only on the restricted core class P_cl(s), which additionally requires zero endpoint changes in bulk kinetic and separately tracked external-field energy. General admitted closed records need not belong to that class, and the reverse record is not explicitly required to belong either. The transfer equations therefore need an explicit domain restriction or supplied extension of these maps.

seams_checked.note: State-coordinate, SI, work-sign, first-law, and tagged-scaling uses match the framework. The reversible-process definition nevertheless evaluates transfer functionals on general admitted closed records although its supplier supplies them only on P_cl(s); see the owning concern. The examples also fail compatibility with the framework's aggregate coordinate composition, as detailed separately.

The derivative definitions and local representation retain the designated open C² charts, SI conversion factors, and positive S_U. Interior exchange equilibrium explicitly assumes attainment and bilateral feasible variations. Concave stability states its convex affine-slice hypotheses and uses the additional common-law cone postulate for the radial Hessian conclusion rather than inferring same-function homogeneity from tagged scaling alone.

The page treats the foundation as macroscopic context. The local entropy-density relation ds/dT=c(T)/T is explicitly an additional continuum postulate, not a consequence attributed to the macroscopic entropy postulate. It expressly avoids identifying the resulting local field with an arbitrary finite-system entropy function.
